newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures take breather after hitting new high.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures take breather after hitting new high.

text.p: German Bund futures continued to build on their two-week old rally on Monday, setting yet another contract high and convincing traders that further gains are likely.
Bond market analysts said the December DTB Bund contract, which was lifted by stronger bond markets elsewhere in Europe, is now targeting a high of 101.36 which was set around the start of the year.
At 1518 GMT, the contract was up 13 basis points at 101.14, but off a high of 101.21 and even with the previous contract high set only last week.

Bunds got a lift from high-yielding debt markets elsewhere in Europe, as was the case earlier in the summer. Italian bonds, for example, sliced eight basis points off the spread against Bunds to 168 basis points.
The spread against Treasuries was fairly steady at 44 basis points.
Analysts said that with few U.S. indicators due this week, the market was turning its attention to German data -- namely the Ifo institute index and M3 data.
Some said they expected the the Ifo index survey, due out later this week, to report a weak figure.
A weak Ifo report would provide the latest in a string of signs that the German economy is not growing as strongly as some had expected and give Bunds a lift.
German M3 money supply data, which has received diminished attention from financial markets of late, is expected again to have a limited impact when it is released later this week.
Analysts said there is almost no way for M3, which grew 8.4 percent in September, to reach the top of its target corridor of seven percent by the end of the year. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
